stem:
Ishaan studies the diagram of square $PQRS$. Dashed segment $PR$ is a diagonal. Grey points $M$, $N$, $O$, $T$ are the midpoints of the sides, joined to form square $MNOT$.

Which plan correctly doubles the area of $PQRS$ and which plan halves it?

options.text: Join the midpoints to double the area, and build on diagonal $PR$ to halve it.
Build a new square on diagonal $PR$ to double the area; join midpoints $M$, $N$, $O$, $T$ to halve it.
Use either construction for either goal, because the starting figure need not be a square.
Treat every inscribed quadrilateral inside $PQRS$ as a half-area square.

teacher.key_rationale: A square on the diagonal has twice the area; the midpoint square has half. Swapping the two plans reverses the constructions; dropping the square start or accepting any inscribed quadrilateral leave the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as square PQRS with diagonal PR and midpoint square MNOT.
